title: How Steve Jobs started NeXT and Pixar: curiosity, paying the bills, and making tech people love without knowing it
summary: Short writings by Steve on the origin of NeXT (a lunch with biochemist Paul Berg), why Pixar's graphics work drew him in, and Pixar's early strategy. He reflects that trying to pay the bills with side products was the wrong approach, and that the goal was technology so good nobody needs to understand it to love the result.

principles.text: Cold-call experts and admit your ignorance; curiosity opens doors to new ideas.
principles.quote: I called him up, and I said, “You remember me. I’m ignorant about this stuff, but I’ve got a bunch of questions about how it works, and I’d love to have lunch with you.”

principles.text: Look for ways technology can speed up and democratize slow expert work.
principles.quote: Not only will it allow you to run your experiments faster, but someday every freshman microbiology student in the country can play with the Paul Berg recombinant software.

principles.text: Seek out people doing work far ahead of anything you've seen.
principles.quote: the stuff that Ed and his team were doing was way ahead of anything I’d ever seen anyone do.

principles.text: Don't dilute focus with side products to pay bills; fund the real work directly.
principles.quote: Probably if you look back in the rearview mirror, we would have been better off just funding the animation efforts and not trying to pay the bills through these other products

principles.text: Make something where nobody needs to understand the technology to love it.
principles.quote: We wanted to use our technology to make something where nobody needed to know anything about the technology to love it. And that’s what we ended up doing.

principles.text: Celebrate team wins and credit collective effort and milestones for the industry.
principles.quote: The computer graphics industry just achieved a major milestone, and Pixar led the way!
